* IMPACTS...Flooding along Raccoon Creek and its tributaries is
occurring. Numerous roads remain closed due to flooding. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

- At 320 PM EDT, county officials reported that flooding of the
Raccoon Creek is occurring across the warned area. State Route
124 in southern Vinton County remains closed due to flooding. In
the City of Vinton, State Route 325 at State Route 160 is closed
due to flooding. State Route 554 between Rio Grande and Bidwell
is closed due to flooding.

continues to slowly rise.

Rio Grande, Vinton, Wilkesville, Adamsville, and Radcliffe.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

properties.description:
FFWFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Gilmer County in north central Georgia...
East Central Murray County in northwestern Georgia...

* Until 700 PM EDT.

* At 302 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Fort Mountain State Park.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 23 at 8:33AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Citrus, Levy and Marion
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 AM EDT Wednesday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain above flood stage at
around 28.2 feet through the next 5 days. Additional rises are
possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
